summary: the start-up velocity of an Oldroyd-B fluid in a planar channel under a suddenly applied pressure gradient, by Waters and King's series

inputs.name: half_width
inputs.meaning: h, the distance from the centreline to a wall, in the length unit of one self-consistent system of units (SI for OpenFOAM)

inputs.name: density
inputs.meaning: rho, mass per volume in that system

inputs.name: solvent_viscosity
inputs.meaning: eta_s, a dynamic viscosity in that system

inputs.name: polymer_viscosity
inputs.meaning: eta_p, a dynamic viscosity in that system

inputs.name: relaxation_time
inputs.meaning: lambda, a time in that system

inputs.name: driving
inputs.meaning: K = -dp/dx, the constant pressure gradient along the channel (force per volume) applied from time zero, in that system

inputs.name: position
inputs.meaning: y, the distance from the centreline at which the velocity is wanted, 0 <= |y| <= h, in the length unit

inputs.name: times
inputs.meaning: the times since the gradient was applied, zero or more, in the time unit

inputs.name: terms
inputs.meaning: how many terms of the series to sum, one or more

outputs.name: velocity
outputs.meaning: pairs [t, u], u the velocity along the channel at the position asked, in the velocity unit of the system

outputs.name: elasticity_number
outputs.meaning: E = lambda eta0 / (rho h^2), eta0 = eta_s + eta_p

outputs.name: steady_mean_velocity
outputs.meaning: K h^2 / (3 eta0), the mean over the channel of the steady velocity, in the velocity unit of the system

validity: an incompressible Oldroyd-B fluid between infinite parallel plates, laminar and one-dimensional, starting from rest with no stress, under a gradient applied as a step; the series converges with the terms as one over the cube of the term's index, and a truncated series does not give zero velocity at t = 0 exactly; a solvent fraction of zero (the upper-convected Maxwell fluid) is within it

source.citation: Amoreira and Oliveira (2010), Comparison of different formulations for the numerical calculation of unsteady incompressible viscoelastic fluid flow, Adv. Appl. Math. Mech. 2(4), 483-502 (read 2026-11-21, https://www.global-sci.com/aamm/article/view/4529; mat-20261121-amoreira-oliveira-2010-startup); OpenFOAM-9, tutorials/incompressible/pimpleFoam/laminar/planarPoiseuille/validation/WatersKing/WatersKing.C (read 2026-11-21; mat-20261121-openfoam-9-planarpoiseuille-watersking)
source.locus: Amoreira and Oliveira, section 2.1, equations (2.5)-(2.9): u/u_mean = (3/2)(1 - y^2) + sum over k of A_k(t) B_k(y), t scaled by lambda1 and y by the half-width h, u_mean = K h^2/(3 eta0), E = lambda1 eta0/(rho h^2); A_k = exp(-b_k t) [((b_k - a_k^2)/c_k) sinh(c_k t) + cosh(c_k t)] if b_k >= a_k and the same with sin and cos if b_k < a_k; B_k = 48 (-1)^k/((2k-1)^3 pi^3) cos((2k-1) pi y/2); a_k = (2k-1) pi sqrt(E)/2, b_k = (1 + beta a_k^2)/2, c_k = sqrt|b_k^2 - a_k^2|; the series is Waters and King's (1970), which this seat did not read. WatersKing.C writes the same terms, with eight of them

note: Written for meta_agent/tasks/034, the reference of the rheoTool agent's start-up channel flow. The hyperbolic branch is computed as exponentials of (c_k - b_k) t and -(c_k + b_k) t, which is the same quantity without overflow at long times. No value of either source stands behind the worked cases (the paper shows its solution as figures): each is worked by hand in its worked field, at long time, where the series has decayed, and at time zero, where the truncated series' sum is a known alternating sum.
